messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: 25OHD levels did not differ significantly between patients treated for depression and healthy controls.
Sentence: "The level of 25OHD and 1,25(OH)2D3 did not differ significantly between the examined groups."
Measured as: depression (patients treated for depression vs healthy controls)
Population: 99 patients aged 46.9 ± 11 years treated for depression and 45 healthy subjects
Intervention: Not applicable (observational; serum 25OHD measured)
Comparator: Healthy controls
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 144
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Each 5-ng/mL higher first-trimester 25(OH)D was associated with lower odds of EPDS-positive postpartum depressive symptoms in the crude model.
Sentence: "Each 5-ng/mL increase in 25(OH)D was associated with lower odds of EPDS-positive symptoms in the crude model (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.25-0.48) and after adjustment for baseline characteristics (adjusted OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.25-0.50)."
Measured as: EPDS-positive postpartum depressive symptoms
Population: 242 women with gestational diabetes mellitus
Intervention: First-trimester serum 25(OH)D concentration (per 5 ng/mL increase)
Comparator: Lower 25(OH)D levels
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 242
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"evaluation":"All three responses reach the same verdict (genuine), the same primary reason (population) and the same also_differs list. The pair is two observational studies on vitamin D and depression, so it is on question; the null case-control finding against the protective cohort finding is genuine, and the population difference (treated depressed adults vs gestational diabetes women with postpartum symptoms) is a sensible primary reason. Differences among them are minor: B gives the most informative rationale and detail, naming both the case-control vs EPDS screen contrast and the control group; C is similar but slightly less specific; A is the thinnest, with a detail that omits the contrast in design and outcome.
